title: Making the Office More Attractive to Team Members
author: Admired Leadership
summary: As organizations push for a return to in-person work, this article argues that leaders need to make the office itself more compelling rather than simply mandating attendance. It cites JP Morgan's multi-billion-dollar New York headquarters, with its restaurants, gym, and after-hours pub, as an extreme example of investing in workplace amenities to win over talent accustomed to remote flexibility. The piece acknowledges most organizations lack those resources but argues that smaller investments in comfort and convenience — coffee bars, soundproof pods, on-site gyms, daycare partnerships — can meaningfully shift how appealing the office feels. The core argument is that comfort and convenience, more than décor, are what actually draw people back in.
points: Many team members have come to view remote-work flexibility as a reward and resist a full return to the office.
JP Morgan's $3 billion NYC headquarters, with multiple restaurants, a gym, and an after-hours pub, illustrates an extreme investment in making the office a destination.
Comfort and convenience matter more than décor — arranging space for both quiet and collaboration is what team members want.
Smaller, achievable investments (coffee bars, soundproof pods, gym subsidies, daycare partnerships) can meaningfully improve the office's appeal.
quotes: Team members have come to view the flexibility of remote work as a reward and are reluctant to give it up.
Consider JP Morgan’s massive $3 billion investment in their New York City Headquarters as a case in point.
The newly constructed 60-story fortress includes a Michelin-starred vegan restaurant, a café serving protein shakes from an Airstream trailer
While lighting, artwork, and issues of décor can make a critical difference, it is comfort and convenience that matter most.
Even small investments in convenience can make a major difference. People like to work where they are most comfortable.
